Dr M Zahir with Khaled Hamid Chowdhury, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner
Abdus Samad Kamal, Advocate ----- For Respondent Nos. 4 & 5.

parties:
Shahajada Talukder ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Election Commissioner and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: 4. Dr M Zahir, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that it is only on four grounds as provided in sub-rule (a)(b)(c) and (d) and (d) of Rule 15(3) of the Rules 1983 that the respondent No.5 could reject the nomination papers filed by the petitioner and that the respondent No. 6 in collusion with the other respondents made the overwriting on the voter numbers of the proposer as well as the petitioner/candidate resulting in variation of the voter number from that of the Electoral Rolls, but such variations in the nomination paper do not come within above sub-rules (a)(b)(c) and (d) of rule 15(3) and further, in terms of section 7(1)(c) of (Union Parishad) Ordinance 1983, hereinafter Ordinance 1983, for the post of chairman of Union Parishad, any candidate whose name appeared on the electoral roll for any ward in the concerned Union was qualified to contest and in the present case the name of the petitioner admittedly appeared on the electoral roll of the concerned ward and so the rejection of the nomination paper on ground of such variation is illegal. Dr Zahir next submits that it is very natural that the petitioner, who earlier was elected chairman consecutively, would not have made such overwriting which resulted in ousting him from the election race and the legal presumption is that the sole beneficiary i.e. the respondent No. 6, who got elected as Chairman uncontested, in collusion with the respondent Nos. 4 and 5 and also other candidates, who later on withdrew their nomination papers so that the proforma respondents No. 6 may get elected uncontested, caused the overwriting in the nomination paper by taking resort to fraud and forgery, while those were under the custody of the respondent No. 5 and then on the plea of variation of voter number got the nomination papers rejected. Further, the declaration of the proforma respondent No. 6 as the uncontested chairman by an antedated order and the publication of the Gazette Notification even after notice of the fact that the High Court Division has granted stay, show the malafide of the respondents.
